Event_Description: White House confirms Apr 2 reciprocal-tariff announcement will proceed and tariffs will be implemented rather than postponed.
"Liberation Day": 10% baseline tariff on most imports plus higher country-specific reciprocal rates (e.g. China 34%, EU 20%, Japan 24%, Vietnam 46%).
Previously announced 25% tariff on imported automobiles takes effect.
Canada announces 25% retaliatory tariffs on selected U.S.-made automobiles, including non-USMCA-compliant vehicles and relevant non-Canadian/non-Mexican content.
China condemns U.S. reciprocal tariffs and says it will resolutely take countermeasures.
China says it has filed a WTO dispute against the U.S. reciprocal tariff measures.
China announces an additional 34% tariff on all U.S. imports, effective Apr 10; also announces rare-earth export controls and other trade restrictions.
The 10% universal baseline tariff announced Apr 2 takes effect.
Trump says markets may have to 'take medicine' and signals no immediate retreat from tariffs.
False report claims Trump is considering a 90-day tariff pause except for China, triggering an abrupt equity rally.
White House denies the purported 90-day tariff pause report and calls it fake news.
Trump says China must withdraw its 34% retaliation by Apr 8 or the U.S. will impose an additional 50% tariff effective Apr 9.
China rejects the U.S. ultimatum and says it will 'fight to the end' rather than withdraw its countermeasures.
White House confirms the additional 50 percentage-point tariff on China will proceed, effective Apr 9.
Canada confirms its 25% retaliatory automobile tariffs will take effect Apr 9.
Formal U.S. action implementing the additional China tariff is published.

Higher country-specific reciprocal tariffs take effect; China's reciprocal component rises to 84%, producing a widely reported 104% incremental 2025 burden when earlier 20% fentanyl tariffs are included.
Canada's 25% retaliatory tariffs on selected U.S.-made automobiles take effect.
China raises its retaliatory tariff on all U.S. goods from 34% to 84%, effective Apr 10, and announces additional entity restrictions.
EU member states approve a first retaliatory package, broadly 25% duties on roughly €21bn of U.S. goods, with first measures due Apr 15.

Trump announces an immediate 90-day pause on higher country-specific reciprocal tariffs for more than 75 countries, reverting them to 10%; China is excluded and its reciprocal tariff is raised to 125%.
Implementation of the Apr 9 pause: most country-specific reciprocal tariffs revert to 10% for 90 days while China remains at sharply elevated rates.
China's 84% retaliatory tariff on all U.S. imports takes effect.

Announcer: European Commission / Ursula von der Leyen
Event_Description: EU announces it will pause its retaliatory tariff package for 90 days to give negotiations a chance.
